steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: GCSE RS focuses on three types of crime: hate crimes, theft and murder. You need to understand religious responses to each type and whether people who break the law for moral reasons should be punished.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Types of Crime
steps.body: 1. For Types of Crime questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Types of Crime to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In the UK, debates about often involve both religious and secular voices. Parliament considers evidence from faith communities alongside scientific, legal and ethical perspectives, reflecting Britain’s commitment to both religious freedom and democratic decision-making.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: The British system of establishing laws through parliamentary debate, judicial interpretation and public consultation allows religious perspectives to be heard alongside other viewpoints. Faith communities regularly submit evidence to parliamentary committees and participate in public consultations on issues related to .

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
